'''''Persicaria capitata''''', the '''pink-headed persicaria''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''pinkhead smartweed''',<ref name=PLANTS>{{PLANTS|id=POCA21|taxon=Polygonum capitatum|accessdate=31 January 2016}}</ref> '''pink knotweed''', Japanese knotweed, or '''pink bubble persicaria''', is <!--[[ornamental plant]] -- no, the wild populations are not ornamentals--> an Asian species of plants in the genus ''[[Persicaria]]'' within the [[Polygonaceae]] (US: buckwheat) family. It is native to Asia (China, South Asia, Indochina)<ref name=lisa/> and grown as an ornamental in other countries. It has become naturalized in [[Australia]], [[South Africa]] and a few scattered locations in the Americas.<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Persicaria%20capitata.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map, ''Persicaria capitata'']</ref><ref name="nswfo"/><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242100091 Flora of North America, ''Persicaria capitata'']</ref>

==Description==
''Persicaria capitata'' is a [[prostrate shrub|prostrate]] herb.<ref name="nswfo">{{cite web|title=Persicaria capitata|url=http://pngplants.org/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Persicaria~capitata|publisher=New South Wales Flora Online|accessdate=2009-07-25}}</ref> The leaves are 1–6 cm long, 0.7–3 cm wide with pink to red bands or blotches and short scattered hairs.<ref name="nswfo" /> The [[Spike (botany)|spikes]] are 5–10 mm long and 5–7 mm in diameter.<ref name=lisa>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242414798 Flora of China, ''Polygonum capitatum'' Buchanan-Hamilton ex D. Don, 1825.  <big>头花蓼</big> tou hua liao ]</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Persicaria capitata'' is a native of Asia. It has naturalised in parts of [[Australia]]<ref name="nswfo" /> and [[North America]].<ref name=PLANTS/> Between 2008 and 2013 it has been recorded as an invasive plant in [[Ireland]] from the Counties [[Fermanagh]], [[Kilkenny]], [[Wexford]] and Mayo.<ref>Devlin, Z. 2017 A new record for the introduced plant ''Persicaria capitata'' (Pink-headed Persicaria), from Newport, Co. Mayo (H27).''Irish Naturalists' Journal'' '''35''':116</ref>

==Uses==
''Persicaria capitata'' has been widely used in [[China]] in the treatment of various urologic disorders including [[urinary calculus|urinary calculi]] and [[urinary tract infections]].<ref>Liao SG, Zhang LJ, Sun F, Zhang JJ, Chen AY, Lan YY, Li YJ, Wang AM, He X, Xiong Y, Dong L, Chen XJ, Li YT, Zuo L, Wang YL, "Antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects of extracts and fractions from ''Polygonum capitatum''."  ''J Ethnopharmacol''. 2011 Feb 3;  Authors:</ref>
